item.title: Hybrid Nanocone-Nanohole Light Trapping for High-Efficiency Thin-Film Silicon Solar Cells
item.description: arXiv:2609.14396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thin-film silicon solar cells exhibit weak absorption at longer wavelengths of visible light due to their limited optical thickness. To overcome this inherent limitation, a hybrid nanocone-nanohole light-management architecture is proposed by integrating front-surface silicon nanocones with embedded air-filled nanoholes in the absorber layer. item.title: Scalable and conformal nickel oxide for efficient perovskite solar modules
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 14 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02012-z A coordination-regulated chemical bath deposition method yields conformal nickel oxide layers for perovskite solar cells, enabling 27.35% certified cell efficiency, 23.42% module efficiency and durable operation.
